notes: COMMITTED CONTRACT SOURCE, and the single source of truth for __LOOPBACK_PORT__ and __APP_SUBNET__. .github/workflows/release.yml reads this document, renders the deployment inputs from its network block, overwrites only the fields a release run can prove, validates the result against release/contract.schema.json, and emits it as release-artifacts/release-contract.json. Every field the workflow does not overwrite is reviewed policy and is authoritative exactly as written here.

acceptance.checks enumerates the COMPLETE published URL space, which is two levels deep: the learning path at /, a home per course (/market-structure-lab/ id course-home, /trade-setup-execution/ id course2-home, /options-trading/ id course3-home), and each course's lessons beneath its own home - one check id per page, 42 pages in all (course 1 lab 01 keeps the id lesson-page; the ids of courses 2 and 3 are course-scoped because a lesson slug is only unique within a course). The two published non-HTML assets, /trade-setup-execution/trade-journal-schema.json (id journal-schema) and /options-trading/options-trade-plan-schema.json (id trade-plan-schema), each have their own check that fetches and PARSES the file rather than asserting page-shaped markers against JSON; a second asset is declared as a second check, never by loosening a page check until both fit it. Every page check demands that page's own full rel=canonical tag: course and lesson paths overlap by prefix and every course home links to all of its lessons, so a bare path substring is satisfied by several documents and proves nothing about which one was served. The seven FLAT /<lesson>/ URLs this site used to serve are retired with no redirect stub behind them; they are deliberately absent here and must not be re-added. tests/test_site_invariants.py REQUIRED_PAGES plus NON_HTML_ASSETS, and the URL tables in scripts/smoke.py, declare the same map against the files on disk and the served responses. Adding a page to one of the three and not the others ships a page nothing checks. application.title stays "Market Structure Lab": it names the app and the image (org.opencontainers.image.title), not the library, which now holds three courses.

Fields only a release run can know carry all-zero sentinels: release_id, source.revision, image.digest, image.reference, build.timestamp, compose.template_sha256, compose.rendered_sha256 and invocation.workflow_run_id. An all-zero digest or revision can never be a real one, so this document can never be mistaken for a release.

network.loopback_port, network.internal_port and network.subnet are UNALLOCATED. The release workflow refuses to render or build while they hold placeholders, and names the allocation gate in the failure. Allocation is a human decision plus a live host preflight (platform-ops docs/APP_ONBOARDING.md section 2 reservation PR, section 4 bootstrap preflight, and docs/EDGE_ROUTING_CONTRACT.md section 5) and must never be automated here.

build.base_images[].digest is __BASE_IMAGE_DIGEST__ because Containerfile.release is the only place a base image is pinned; the workflow copies the digests it actually built from there, so the two can never drift.
placeholders_present is true, so every release gate must refuse this document as it stands.

The trade journal exchange schema is served as JSON at /trade-setup-execution/trade-journal-schema.json, parses, and declares the trade-journal-v1 shape lesson 14 exports and lesson 15 imports. A 200 alone would not prove any of that.

The options trade plan schema is served as JSON at /options-trading/options-trade-plan-schema.json, parses, and declares the options-trade-plan-v1 shape course 3 lesson 16 exports. A 200 alone proves none of that; a page-shaped marker would prove less.
An unknown path returns a real 404 and never a soft 200 or a redirect to the index.

Served HTML references no origin other than its own; only data: URIs and non-fetching XML namespaces are exempt. Applied to EVERY published page - the learning path, both course homes and all 22 lessons - not just the path named here.
Application security header policy is present on HTML responses.
